pages.text: In the morning, Mom went to the paddy with a basket on her head. A long pole still held the apron she had hung there before. She set Dingding's bamboo hat on the pole, too.
The sun climbed high. "I need my hat for the paddy," Dingding said. But the hat was gone.
Mom searched the room. "Where could it be?"
She opened the wooden box. There were only balls of thread inside.
She looked behind the door. "I had it in my hand this morning."
The sun was hot. Dingding's forehead felt hot, too.
From the yard, Dingding looked down at the paddy. There was the hat, on the pole!
"Mom! My hat is scaring the birds away!" Mom looked down from the bank.
Dingding gently lifted the hat off the pole. One sparrow flew out. It seemed to have been napping inside.
